name: Mohammed bin Salman Al Saud
role: Crown Prince and Prime Minister of Saudi Arabia (crown prince since 2017, prime minister since 2022); de facto ruler
summary: Mohammed bin Salman leads Saudi Arabia as an authoritarian monarchy while driving economic diversification through Vision 2030, privatisation and the Public Investment Fund. He has cut the powers of the religious police and clerics, ended the driving ban and loosened guardianship, while keeping Islam as the constitutional basis and jailing critics. In foreign policy he is hostile to Iran, close to the US, open to Israeli normalisation tied to a Palestinian state, and says Saudi Arabia would seek nuclear weapons if Iran did.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: He is a major arms buyer and plans to produce half of military equipment needs at home.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: He defended hereditary monarchy as the basis of Saudi Arabia and said changing it would betray the Al Saud and thousands of tribal leaders.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Vision 2030 aims to raise the non-profit sector from under 1% to 5% of GDP and give it a larger role in health, education and housing, though it does not say charities outperform state programmes.

clerical-rule.rationale: He said the head of the Islamic establishment is the ruler, the final fatwa is the king's, and the mufti and Fatwa Board are only advisers.

close-ties-china.rationale: The Strategic Defense Agreement he signed with the United States states that the Kingdom views the United States as its primary strategic partner and brings F-35 and tank purchases.

collective-defense.rationale: He signed the 2025 Strategic Mutual Defense Agreement with Pakistan stating that any aggression against either country is aggression against both.

cut-consumption-tax.rationale: His government introduced VAT and excise taxes on sugary drinks and energy drinks and he said in 2018 that this tax reform was done.

death-penalty.rationale: Executions are carried out under his premiership at a high rate, with 345 in 2024 and 286 for terrorism-related offences between 2014 and mid-2025, according to Amnesty International.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: He said constitutional monarchy would not work in Saudi Arabia, which is based on pure monarchy, and that changing the system would betray the Al Saud and tribal leaders.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: He said women can work in any sector, that the Prophet's wife was a businesswoman, and that women and men are equal human beings; the guardianship rules date from 1979 and could be changed.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: In 2021 he announced net zero by 2060 and a cut of 278 Mt a year by 2030, but through a circular carbon economy that keeps oil's role, and in 2018 he said electric vehicles pose no risk to oil.

dynastic-succession.rationale: He said Saudi Arabia is a monarchy founded on the royal family and Allegiance Council, that changing it would betray the Al Saud, and that the king chooses the crown prince.

elective-rulers.rationale: He said constitutional monarchy would not work in Saudi Arabia, which is based on pure monarchy with its tribal and royal structure.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: He signed a mutual defence pact with Pakistan in 2025 under which aggression against one is aggression against both, and a Strategic Defense Agreement with the United States.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: He has said Saudi Arabia keeps spare oil capacity and will supply the market as needed, and expects oil demand to keep rising for some years; this sits alongside diversification and renewables targets.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Vision 2030 promises to extend non-Saudis' ability to own real estate in certain areas, which rejects a blanket ban, though ownership stays limited.

free-public-college.rationale: He said the basic system of governance stipulates that health and education services are free for every citizen.

gradual-change.rationale: He asked the world for time on women's rights, citing the slow US path to women's suffrage, and said change comes without civil war, yet his own reforms have been rapid and top-down.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: He said Saudi Arabia does not want a nuclear bomb but, if Iran develops one, would follow suit as soon as possible; he gave this position in 2018 and repeated it later.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: He said Israelis and Palestinians both have the right to live and coexist, and that Israel is not an enemy but a potential ally; no opened source has him address a Jewish state or the Land of Israel.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Vision 2030 calls for a country with Islam as its constitution, and he said reforms go forward without leaving Saudi laws based on religion.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Under his premiership Saudi Arabia lifted its drug-execution moratorium in November 2022 and executed 122 people for drug offences in 2024, according to Amnesty International.

limit-growth.rationale: Vision 2030 and his interviews set rapid growth as a goal: a larger economy, more jobs and non-oil revenue, and he said the economy would grow almost 7 percent.

local-essentials-public.rationale: He said in 2018 that over twenty services would be privatised in 2019, most of them in water, agriculture and energy, and Vision 2030 corporatises hospitals for later privatisation.

military-superiority.rationale: His government agreed to buy F-35 aircraft and nearly 300 tanks from the United States, a Strategic Defense Agreement with it, and signed a mutual defence pact with Pakistan.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Vision 2030 sets out delivery of health, education, housing and municipal services through public corporations, private firms and the non-profit sector, with competition among providers and citizen choice of provider.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-11): its rationale is about a monarch who rules, and the statement now asks only about a ceremonial head of state, on which the sources cited here are silent.

more-religion-public.rationale: He said Saudi Arabia was not like this before 1979 and that extremists changed the religion, and that the country is returning to the open practice of the Prophet's time and of Saudi Arabia before 1979.

national-resource-control.rationale: He said Aramco and Sabic remain majority-owned by the state fund with only a small share listed, and Vision 2030 commits to continue localising the oil and gas sector.

national-self-determination.rationale: He backs a Palestinian state on the 1967 borders with East Jerusalem as capital, which concerns one people and does not state that every people has a right to a state.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-11): its rationale is about one government, party or regime, or about fighting corruption, not a general claim that most politicians put their own interests first, which this statement now asks.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Vision 2030 commits to complete the GCC common market, unifying customs, economic and legal policies.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Vision 2030 commits to strengthen, preserve and highlight national identity, uphold Arabic and restore heritage sites.

priority-to-poor.rationale: He said his focus is on citizens earning 3,000 to 7,000 riyals who hold poor jobs, though he also named stable state finances as a first priority.

property-fundamental.rationale: A committee he headed was given powers to arrest, impose travel bans and seize assets apparently without judicial review, and in November 2017 held princes, officials and businessmen at the Ritz-Carlton until they settled by handing over assets.

public-ownership.rationale: He is selling shares in Aramco and moving water, energy and other services to private operators, but said Aramco and Sabic stay majority-owned by the state fund, so the evidence is mixed.

reduce-immigration.rationale: He said more than 10 million foreigners live in Saudi Arabia, that the number will not decrease but increase because the economy needs workers, and that tourism will create jobs for expatriates.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: He said there are no fixed schools of thought and no infallible person, that interpretation of the Quran and Sunnah stays open, and that fatwas must reflect the time, place and mindset in which they are issued.

religious-nation.rationale: Vision 2030 names Islamic faith and national unity as what make the nation exceptional, yet he also says the country is open to all religions.

restore-past-order.rationale: He frames reform as a return to the Saudi Arabia of before 1979, but pairs it with a technology-driven future; no source weighs restoration against progress.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Asked whether reforms could have come without the Ritz-Carlton detentions and curbs on public dissent, he said it was the only way and a decision between bad and worse for the nation.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: The killers of Jamal Khashoggi were tried behind closed doors, with the accused, their roles and the charges undisclosed, according to the UN rapporteur, so the record shows no open legal accountability.

separate-church-state.rationale: Vision 2030 describes Islam as the constitution and Islamic principles as the driving force of the state, though he has cut clerical powers within that framework.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: The Personal Status Law he promoted requires wives to obey their husbands in a reasonable manner and makes maintenance depend on obedience, according to Human Rights Watch.

state-directs-investment.rationale: He restructured the Public Investment Fund to steer capital into chosen sectors (renewables, industry, real estate, a transformed Aramco) and Vision 2030 names the strategic sectors and localisation targets the state will pursue.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: He signed a Strategic Defense Agreement with the United States that affirms the Kingdom views it as its primary strategic partner, with F-35 and tank purchases.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: He said the mufti and the fatwa board are advisers to the king, who has the final word, and that muftis must be regulated and certified by the government.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Freedom House reports arrests and long prison terms for peaceful criticism, including a 23-year sentence for a cartoonist in 2024, and Human Rights Watch reports a death sentence for social media posts under a 2017 law placing prosecution and security bodies under the royal court.

targeted-social-spending.rationale: Vision 2030 says subsidies for fuel, food, water and electricity will be redirected towards those in need rather than provided to all.

tech-with-ancestral-values.rationale: Vision 2030 says its technology-led plan will be achieved by adhering closely to Islamic principles, Arab values and national traditions, and in 2017 he paired a return to the past with a technology-driven future.

torture-always-illegal.rationale: He said Islam forbids torture and that Saudi laws forbid torture.

traditional-family.rationale: Vision 2030 states that families are the key building block of society, protecting it from social breakdown, and names Islamic values and extended family ties as defining Saudi traits.

universal-healthcare.rationale: He said the basic system of governance stipulates free health care for every citizen, and also that government hospitals will move to private and non-profit providers and employees will hold insurance policies.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: He campaigns against extremist ideologies and said extremists distort Islam; he has also fought Islamist movements that reject rulers.

wife-divorce-without-consent.rationale: Under the law he promoted a husband can divorce unilaterally while a wife can only petition a court on limited grounds and must establish harm, according to Human Rights Watch.

women-must-cover.rationale: He said Sharia requires decent, respectful clothing for women like men, that it does not specify a black abaya or head cover, and that the choice of attire is left to women.

women-suffrage.rationale: He pointed to women voting and winning seats in the 2015 municipal elections and said women can work in any sector, including politics, adding that more time is needed; Saudi Arabia still has no national elections.

notes: Later pass under rules 7. Primary texts read in full: Atlantic 2022, Al-Mudaifer 2021, TIME 2018, 60 Minutes 2018, CBS 2019, Bloomberg 2016 and 2018, Economist 2016, Vision 2030, the 2017 FII and 2021 SGI speeches, and the 2024 summit and Shura Council speeches as reported. Record (executions, the Personal Status Law, detentions, defence agreements, trials) is cited from reports of it and answers alone where it exists. Themes searched: economy, liberty, society, government, world, ecology, means and culture; most economy, technology and means statements have no stated position of his. He is shown only if the uncertainty rule passes. Positions on Israel moved: 2018 coexistence and a Palestinian state, 2022 potential ally, 2023 closer to normalisation, 2024 no relations without a Palestinian state; the Israel answers that rested on Wikipedia were nulled. The earlier answers that cited Wikipedia (s8) and an NPR summary (s9) were revised or nulled; they remain listed only as sources of leads.
